subject: Proposal: short-term SLA adjustment for filter-mediated tool-call latency
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@orionfin.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency spikes from content-filtered tool calls — impact to our SLA

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Quick note from our side — over the last 72 hours we've observed intermittent 600-1200ms additional per-request latency when our calls trigger Redwood's content filter + downstream tool invocation path for structured payouts. Rough summary: about 0.8% of requests experience the extra delay, but when they do it sometimes pushes end-to-end p95 above our committed 1200ms.

This is visible in our tracing and we've attached a short log extract (slo-impact-metrics.csv) showing the correlation between content classification decisions and tool-call handoffs. We're concerned this will cause a breach on our monthly SLA if pattern persists while you roll out the mitigation you mentioned in last week's sync.

Request: would Redwood consider a short-term carve-out / SLA adjustment for latency attributable to content-filter-triggered tool invocations until a telemetry-based attribution and mitigation are in place? If so, we need:
- Clear measurement window and attribution criteria (how you will count/exclude requests)
- Expected timeline for mitigation (patch / model update / routing change)
- Any compensatory credits if regression continues past the window

Happy to jump on a 30m call today. We need to get procurement and our SREs aligned on acceptance language.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of Platform Engineering, Orion Financials
attachments: slo-impact-metrics.csv (excerpt)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@orionfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spikes from content-filtered tool calls — impact to our SLA

Jordan — thanks for the signal and for the sample traces, that made it clear. We're treating this as priority P1 for accounts where structured tool-calls are on the critical path.

Quick operational proposal so everyone has a concrete path forward:
1) Temporary carve-out: Redwood can exclude requests from monthly latency SLO calculations where the additional tail is demonstrably caused by synchronous content-filter classification + external tool invocation.
   - Attribution: use the filter decision flag + tool-call start timestamp to link the extra latency. We'll provide a deterministic rule (example: requests where filter_decision != \"pass\" AND downstream_tool_start - request_start > 200ms).
2) Measurement window: 14 calendar days starting when we enable higher-fidelity telemetry for your org (we can enable by EOD tomorrow). During that period we'll monitor and provide daily reports.
3) Mitigation timeline: engineering plan targets a staged mitigation (routing tweaks + cache warmup + filter model micro-optimizations) over 7 business days; full rollback/fallback logic expected within 10 business days if regressions persist.
4) Compensation guardrail: if after 14 days the measurable rate of excluded requests still causes 5%+ monthly p95 delta vs baseline, we'll discuss a targeted credit formula.

I've attached a short draft of the exemption MPO (proposed-exemption-mpo.docx) for legal/procurement read. Marissa — can you confirm the legal/PS checklist items we'll need to finalize this with Orion? Ben / Laura, please confirm telemetry fields we require so Jordan's SREs can validate instrumentation on their side.

If that looks reasonable to you, Jordan, we can spin up a 30-minute call and include GuardShield's compliance contact (see below) to confirm the audit approach.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Director, Customer Success & Reliability, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-exemption-mpo.docx

Jordan / Avery — looping in a short SLO amendment draft and the metrics extract we discussed. I've attached the CSV with per-request markers and a simple aggregation that shows the delta when the filter path is engaged.

Draft SLO language (summary):
"Redwood agrees to exclude from latency SLO calculations any end-to-end request latency that is demonstrably attributable to synchronous content classification and external tool invocation where the classification outcome triggers a tool call. Attribution will be performed according to the mutually agreed instrumentation rules and will be limited to a 14-calendar-day evaluation window starting when high-fidelity telemetry is enabled for the customer's tenancy."

Operational notes:
- We need Orion to validate traces contain the following fields: request_id, filter_decision, tool_invocation_start, tool_invocation_duration, redwood_node_id. (Ben, please confirm minimal schema.)
- Legal: proposed-exemption-mpo.docx has a short clause around measurement and an acceptance sign-off that Jordan's procurement can countersign.

Next steps:
- Jordan: confirm acceptance of the 14-day window and whether Orion needs any bilateral audit language (GuardShield can attest classification chain if you want).
- Ben: confirm telemetry fields and whether we can flip on the higher-resolution instrumentation for Orion's tenancy by EOD tomorrow.
- Laura: please draft a one-paragraph amendment for the renewal SOW if we decide to persist this change beyond the evaluation window.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks for looping us in. GuardShield can provide a narrow, one-time classification audit to confirm whether the filter decisions correlate with the tool invocations in your sample set. We typically need the following to start:
- A 7-day log window (S3 access or secure upload) with request_id, timestamp, filter_label, and the tool invocation marker.
- A signed data processing addendum (we can operate under your existing agreement if you prefer).

We can deliver an initial correlation report within 2 business days of receiving logs, and a brief remediation checklist if we see classifier-induced latency patterns. We'll also provide a small attestation PDF you can attach to the exemption MPO.

Jordan — if you can provide a sample upload link and confirm the DPA path, we can kick this off today.

Best,
